What if you slept with the lights on every night?

Lots of people leave a lamp on because the dark feels scary, or they fall asleep reading. Your brain uses darkness to release melatonin, the sleep hormone. Light hitting your eyes tells your brain it's still daytime, even through closed eyelids.

But here's the twist. A study found that sleeping with moderate light for just one night raised heart rate and blood sugar levels the next morning! Experts say keep your bedroom as dark as you can, and use a dim red night light if you need one.
